name: Thyme
classification_notes: A humanist serif that swaps traditional serifs for gently flared terminals, following Caslon's proportions but softened. The large x-height and moderate contrast keep it working at both text and display sizes.
summary: A seven-weight flare serif that trades sharp serifs for soft, rounded terminals, giving Caslon's proportions a friendlier voice.
description: Thyme takes Caslon's timeless proportions and reworks the serifs into gentle flares, producing a warmer, more approachable text face without losing its structure. Seven weights from Light to Heavy come with a variable font, and the moderate contrast holds up in both long-form text and packaging or brand work.
foundry_blurb: Typeverything position Thyme as a humanist flare serif meant to bring warmth and personality to contemporary typography, citing Caslon as its structural reference. They recommend it for packaging, editorial design and full brand systems, praising its readability at both display and text sizes.

name: Truly
classification_notes: A chunky, soft-curved display sans drawing on 1968 flower-power advertising lettering. Rounded, playful forms and a full italic pairing put it in the retro-display bracket rather than a neutral text sans.
summary: A seven-weight retro display sans with soft curves and chunky forms, built to carry the optimism of late-1960s advertising lettering.
description: Truly borrows its bold, rounded rhythm from a 1968 advertising campaign, giving it a nostalgic yet clearly contemporary character. Soft curves and generous chunky forms suit children's branding, food packaging and playful logotypes. Seven weights come in both upright and italic, bundled into a single variable font.
foundry_blurb: Typeverything describe Truly as inspired by bold 1968 display lettering, aiming to capture flower-power optimism with a modern twist. They pitch it at children's brands, food packaging, toys and any project wanting a friendly, retro-charged voice.

name: Catch
classification_notes: A playful reverse-contrast sans with unconventional weight distribution across strokes. The quirky proportions place it in display use rather than neutral text setting.
summary: A six-weight reverse-contrast sans with exaggerated, quirky proportions built for cheerful, attention-grabbing branding.
description: Catch flips the usual stroke logic of a sans, giving it unconventional proportions and a lively, energetic texture. It suits kids' branding, food packaging and playful identity work where personality matters more than restraint. Six weights ship alongside a variable font for flexible display use.
foundry_blurb: Typeverything call Catch a playful reverse-contrast sans built for warmth and fun, aimed at kids' branding, food packaging and vibrant visual systems that need an energetic, approachable voice.

name: Wrangler
classification_notes: A bold single-weight script inspired by vintage neon shop signage rather than classic brush calligraphy. Swashy capitals and stylistic alternates support logotype and signage use.
summary: A bold signage-style script inspired by vintage German neon shop signs, with swashy capitals for confident wordmarks.
description: Wrangler channels the flowing, hand-painted lettering found on old neon shop signage rather than classic baseball script, though it shares some of that same confidence. Expressive curves and a generous set of swash alternates make it well suited to logos, beer labels and storefront branding. It ships as a single bold weight with full Latin Extended support.
foundry_blurb: Typeverything describe Wrangler as a bold script rooted in vintage German neon signage, built for logos, packaging, sports graphics and storefront branding, with stylistic alternates and swashy uppercase letters for distinctive wordmarks.

name: Tuffo
classification_notes: A warm brush script referencing vintage Italian bodega and shop signage, offered across six weights with a variable font. Swashy uppercase alternates support logotype work.
summary: A six-weight brush script inspired by vintage Italian bodega signs, running from light and delicate to heavy and juicy.
description: Tuffo takes its rhythm from the expressive brush lettering of old Italian bodega signage and packaging, named after the Italian word for dive. Six weights interpolate through a variable font, from spirited lighter cuts to dense display weights, with swashy uppercase alternates adding extra flair.
foundry_blurb: Typeverything present Tuffo as a fun display script drawing on vintage Italian bodega signs and packaging, pitched at food brands, restaurants and playful identities that want nostalgic charm with modern usability.

name: Odiseo
classification_notes: A high-impact serif built around sharp angular cuts and pointed terminals, referencing Greek mythology and classical inscriptions. Heavy proportions push it toward display and headline use.
summary: A seven-style angular serif with pointed terminals and heavy proportions, built for headline and sports-adjacent display work.
description: Odiseo channels classical inscription and Greek myth through sharp, angular cuts and pointed terminals rather than soft classical curves. Heavy proportions and a sculpted silhouette give it presence in branding, sports graphics, film titling and posters. It comes in seven styles and a variable font, with Latin Extended support for multilingual projects.
foundry_blurb: Typeverything describe Odiseo as a powerful serif built for impact, drawing on ancient heroism and classical inscriptions while staying contemporary. They position it for branding, sports graphics, movie titles and large-scale campaigns.

name: Bronco
classification_notes: A bold comic-inspired sans referencing 'Kapow' and 'Bang' style lettering, with a second cursive-leaning alternate set built into the same system.
summary: A five-weight comic-inspired sans with a built-in cursive alternate set that shifts the tone from punchy to playful.
description: Bronco takes the punchy, expressive energy of comic-book sound effects and refines it into a working sans system. A set of loose, almost-connected alternate characters sits alongside the core style, letting designers dial the tone from bold impact toward softer, quirkier compositions. Five weights and a variable font cover the range, with full Latin Extended support.
foundry_blurb: Typeverything describe Bronco as comic-book energy refined into a type system, inspired by classic 'Kapow' and 'Bang' lettering, and recommend it for food, kids and entertainment branding that wants character and movement.

name: Serva
classification_notes: Takes Caslon's old-style structure and simplifies the details, tightening terminals and moderating contrast for a cleaner, more contemporary serif suited to both branding and editorial text.
summary: A seven-weight old-style serif that reduces Caslon's details to a sharper, more deliberate contemporary structure.
description: Serva reworks Caslon's old-style foundations through reduction: simplified details, tightened terminals and carefully managed contrast produce a familiar but more controlled texture. Seven weights and a variable axis adapt it from spacious display use to denser editorial settings, aimed at modern branding and editorial systems that value consistency over flourish.
foundry_blurb: Typeverything describe Serva as Caslon's foundations refined through reduction and control, built for modern branding and editorial systems where clarity and tone matter more than stylistic excess.

name: Atera
classification_notes: A geometric sans rooted in Futura's modernist clarity, softened with rounded forms and ball terminals. A parallel Art Nouveau alternate set adds an expressive second voice within the same family.
summary: A seven-weight geometric sans that softens Futura's clarity with rounded ball terminals, plus a full Art Nouveau alternate set for a more ornamental voice.
description: Atera reinterprets early modernist geometric sans design through a warmer, more human lens, using gently rounded forms and ball terminals to soften strict geometry. Seven weights and a variable font cover confident headline and editorial use, while an extensive Art Nouveau-inflected alternate set lets the same family shift from structured to fluid and ornamental.
foundry_blurb: Typeverything describe Atera as a geometric sans with a soft voice, rooted in the clarity of early modernist typefaces but reinterpreted through a more approachable, contemporary lens with rich alternates.

name: Graphics
classification_notes: A single heavy-weight monolinear display sans rooted in 1970s graphic culture, with tightly packed, modular letterforms and small cut-in details.
summary: A single heavyweight modular display sans built from tightly packed, monolinear letterforms with a strong 1970s poster feel.
description: Graphics leans on the visual culture of 1970s design magazines and disco posters, built as one confident heavy weight with a minimal, modular structure. Small cut-in details add rhythm without breaking the solid, dense letterforms, giving it real presence in posters, logotypes and bold headline work.
foundry_blurb: Typeverything describe Graphics as a bold, high-impact display typeface rooted in 1970s visual culture, built as a single heavy style for posters, logotypes and book covers, with a modular, monolinear structure.

name: Groto
classification_notes: A grotesque sans drawing on early American woodtype and Franklin-style display grotesques, with an extensive vintage-leaning alternate set alongside a cleaner default character set.
summary: An eight-weight grotesque sans with roots in early American woodtype, offering a clean default alongside a full set of vintage-leaning alternates.
description: Groto draws its bold, slightly mischievous character from Franklin-style grotesques and nineteenth-century woodtype display faces. The default character set is a clean contemporary read, while an extensive alternate collection unlocks a more classical, vintage-inspired look. Eight weights and a variable font cover branding, packaging and editorial headline use.
foundry_blurb: Typeverything describe Groto as a characterful sans inspired by the energy of early woodtype grotesques, refined for modern use while keeping its bold impact and open, slightly playful shapes.

name: Athos
classification_notes: A workhorse grotesque built for screens and interfaces rather than headline display: tabular figures, math support and a Text weight tuned for dark backgrounds all point to UI and product use.
summary: A seven-weight screen-first grotesque with icon support and a dark-mode-tuned Text weight, built for interfaces and dense data over headline display.
description: Athos is built as a practical tool for interfaces and communication design rather than a display statement. Seven weights and a variable font include a dedicated Text weight tuned for dark backgrounds, alongside a small icon set for packaging, transport and UI use. Full Latin Extended coverage, tabular figures and math support suit dashboards and long-form paragraphs alike.
foundry_blurb: Typeverything pitch Athos as a practical tool typeface built for screens and real work, combining full language coverage, ligatures, tabular numerals and math support with an icon set for interface and packaging use.

name: Edite
classification_notes: A contemporary take on De Vinne, the 1890s transitional serif, refined for sharper geometry and modern clarity. Nine weights each with true italics push it toward branding and editorial use.
summary: An eighteen-style transitional serif reworking the 1890s De Vinne model with sharper cuts and a full set of true italics.
description: Edite began as a search for a contemporary De Vinne, keeping that 1890s serif's spirit while adding the geometry and clarity modern use demands. Nine weights in upright and italic, both with variable files, give it real range, and a friendlier alternate set on the uprights adds versatility for branding and editorial work. Sharp cuts and subtle angular geometry keep its tone confident.
foundry_blurb: Typeverything describe Edite as their take on a contemporary De Vinne, a classic 1890s serif, refined with sharp cuts and confident geometry for print, packaging and visual identity work, with a particularly well-regarded italic.

name: Brave
classification_notes: A revival of Bernhard Black (1928), a preliminary design that preceded Bernhard Block, reworked into a full contemporary sans system with ten weights, italics and an extra Poster weight.
summary: A twenty-style sans reviving the little-known 1928 Bernhard Black, with ten weights, full italics and an extra Poster cut for headline use.
description: Brave rebuilds Bernhard Black, a 1928 design that preceded the better-known Bernhard Block, keeping the bold stance and subtly angled stems that gave it warmth. Ten weights from Thin to Poster, each with a matching italic, balance early-twentieth-century strength with contemporary polish, suited to branding, packaging, editorial layouts and extended text alike.
foundry_blurb: Typeverything describe Brave as a contemporary reinterpretation of Bernhard Black, an overlooked 1928 design whose bold, angled stems felt worth reviving. They built it into a full sans family for branding, packaging and editorial use.

name: Crunch
classification_notes: A cheerful, dense display sans drawing on mid-century British grotesques Gill Kayo and Antique Olive, with a heavy master built for packaging shelf presence and a set of decorative alternates.
summary: An eight-style display sans built from mid-century British grotesque roots, with a heavy master designed to pop off a shelf and a playful set of decorative alternates.
description: Crunch draws its density from Gill Kayo and its warmth from Antique Olive, reinterpreting both through a joyful, contemporary lens. Eight styles and a variable font move from light and expressive to the compact, powerful heavy master that anchors the family. A generous alternate set swaps in flowers, smileys and stars for playful packaging and kids' branding.
foundry_blurb: Typeverything describe Crunch as a cheerful, high-impact display family inspired by mid-century British grotesques, built for fun packaging, kids' products and creative campaigns, with a set of playful alternate glyphs.

name: Deia
classification_notes: A bracketed serif sitting between traditional and modern models, now in its 2.0 revision with true italics designed as companions rather than simple slants.
summary: An eight-weight bracketed serif with true companion italics, calm in structure but confident enough for fashion and beverage branding.
description: Deia sits between traditional and modern serif models, its softly shaped serifs giving it a calm authority rather than either strict classicism or hard modernity. Now updated to version 2.0, it gains fluid true italics designed as genuine companions to the uprights. Eight weights with matching italics, plus a variable font in the full desktop family, suit packaging and branding in fashion, lifestyle and beverage projects.
foundry_blurb: Typeverything describe Deia as a contemporary bracketed serif reworked for improved rhythm and screen performance in its 2.0 release, with new true italics designed as companions rather than slanted counterparts.

name: Berry
classification_notes: A friendly flare serif with soft curves and open shapes, sharing its structural family with Ready but marketed and described separately by the foundry.
summary: An eight-style flare serif with soft curves and generous proportions, built for fashion, food and lifestyle branding that wants warmth with confidence.
description: Berry pairs soft curves and gently flared details with generous proportions, sitting between classic charm and contemporary clarity. Its strong presence suits fashion, food, lifestyle and pet brands looking for a distinctive, human voice. Eight styles and a variable font cover everything from logotypes and headlines to packaging and short-form copy.
foundry_blurb: Typeverything describe Berry as a friendly flare serif built for brands wanting warmth and confidence, recommending it across fashion, food, lifestyle and pet branding for its soft edge and generous presence.

name: Archie Brackett
classification_notes: A bold, fixed-width semi-serif in the Copperplate tradition, offered as a single confident weight with an extensive swash alternate system rather than a weight range.
summary: A single-weight fixed-width semi-serif with Copperplate-adjacent proportions and an extensive swash alternate system for posters and headline work.
description: Archie Brackett balances formality with a willingness to bend the rules, built as one confident fixed-width weight rather than a full range. Swashy uppercase and lowercase alternates open up dozens of visual directions from a single style, giving it real range in posters, campaigns and large-scale typography where character matters as much as clarity.
foundry_blurb: Typeverything describe Archie Brackett as a bold, fixed-width semi-serif sitting in the same typographic neighbourhood as Copperplate, built as a single weight with an extensive swash alternate system for expressive display work.

name: Mapamond
classification_notes: A narrow, contemporary interpretation of the Garamond tradition redesigned for screen use, with matching romans and richly equipped italics.
summary: A fourteen-style narrow serif reworking the Garamond tradition for screen use, with an especially richly equipped italic.
description: Mapamond narrows the classical Garamond model into a crisp, efficient texture built to perform on screen as well as in print. Seven weights with matching romans and italics, all available as variable fonts, cover branding and communication systems. The italic in particular carries an extensive set of alternates, ligatures and swashes for logos and editorial headlines.
foundry_blurb: Typeverything describe Mapamond as a contemporary, narrow interpretation of the Garamond tradition redesigned for modern screen use, balancing classical proportions with a crisp, efficient texture for branding and editorial work.

name: Olivo
classification_notes: A contemporary reinterpretation of Antique Olive, adjusting the original's reverse-contrast logic and proportions for digital use rather than print.
summary: A sixteen-style reworking of Antique Olive, adjusting its distinctive reverse-contrast logic for confident performance on screen.
description: Olivo revisits Antique Olive's contrast logic, which read well in print but needed adjustment for digital environments, retuning proportions and rhythm for contemporary media. Sixteen styles and a variable font bridge mid-century character with modern clarity, suited to branding, display and text use alike.
foundry_blurb: Typeverything describe Olivo as a contemporary reinterpretation of the iconic Antique Olive, revisited with today's visual language in mind and reworked so its once print-specific contrast performs well across contemporary media.

name: Delwe Serif
classification_notes: One of two families sold under the Delwe tile: a modern serif revival of Letraset's Belwe, stripped of its Venetian detailing for a cleaner, more functional structure. Bundled with a separate Slab family; split here as the two are genuinely different categories.
summary: A nine-weight modern serif reviving Letraset's Belwe, with the original's Venetian detailing removed for a cleaner, more functional structure.
description: Delwe Serif takes Belwe as its starting point and streamlines it, dropping the Venetian details in favour of clean, sturdy letterforms optimised for screens. Balanced proportions keep it reliable across both display headlines and extended text, with a friendly tone suited to editorial content and confident branding. Nine weights from Thin to Heavy come with a variable font.
foundry_blurb: Typeverything describe Delwe as a modern slab and serif revival of Letraset's Belwe. The Serif family keeps the original's spirit while removing its Venetian detailing for a more streamlined, functional design built for both display and extended text.

name: Delwe Slab
classification_notes: The slab counterpart bundled with Delwe's Serif family, sharing the same nine-weight structure but built with slab-serif proportions and stylistic alternates that nod to Belwe's historical origins.
summary: A nine-weight slab serif companion to Delwe Serif, adding stylistic alternates that nod back to its Belwe origins.
description: Delwe Slab shares its structure and weight range with the Serif family but shifts into slab-serif proportions, sturdy and clean enough for both headlines and longer text. A set of stylistic alternates nods to Belwe's historical detailing, giving designers extra flexibility for distinctive branding or editorial layouts. Nine weights ship with a variable font.
foundry_blurb: Typeverything describe the Slab half of Delwe as carrying stylistic alternates that nod to its historical Belwe origins, giving it extra flexibility for distinctive visual identities and editorial layouts alongside its Serif sibling.

name: Forta
classification_notes: A humanist workhorse sans built across three widths (Condensed, Normal, Wide), each with a full weight and italic range, positioning it as a general-purpose system rather than a display face.
summary: A humanist workhorse sans spanning three widths and a full weight-and-italic range, built as a flexible general-purpose system.
description: Forta is designed as a versatile workhorse rather than a display statement, offered across Condensed, Normal and Wide widths with matching weights and italics in each. Finely tuned letterforms balance personality with clarity, suited to branding, packaging, titling, editorial design and web use.
foundry_blurb: Typeverything describe Forta as a new humanist sans-serif designed to excel as a versatile workhorse, offering unmatched flexibility across its widths and styles for branding, packaging, titles and editorial design.

name: Raporte
classification_notes: A brush script referencing the 1938 metal typeface Reporter, rebuilt from a stripped-back neon-sign version with blunter, more monoline endings and heavy use of automatic OpenType alternation.
summary: A single-weight brush script rebuilding the 1938 classic Reporter from a stripped-back neon-sign reading, with hundreds of automatic alternates so repeated letters never look cloned.
description: Raporte traces back to Reporter, a 1938 brush script cast by Norddeutsche Schriftgiesserei, but takes its cue from a German neon sign where the texture had worn down to blunt, near-monoline strokes. Rebuilt with contemporary tools, it leans on OpenType alternation so repeated letters vary automatically, with hundreds of possible ligature connections. It suits logos, book and magazine titling, posters and packaging.
foundry_blurb: Typeverything describe Raporte as inspired by the classic 1938 script Reporter, rebuilt from a weathered neon-sign version of the design with blunter, more contemporary strokes and extensive automatic alternates.

name: Claro
classification_notes: A wide, bold grotesque drawing on 1890s New York truck lettering, with humanist details softening its otherwise rugged, sporty proportions. Two families cover upright and italic.
summary: An eighteen-style wide grotesque with a rugged, sporty edge, drawn from 1890s New York truck lettering and softened with humanist detailing.
description: Claro takes its bold, masculine stance from the rugged grotesque lettering seen on New York trucks in the 1890s, blending that historical grit with modern precision. Wider-than-usual proportions give it strength, while subtle humanist details keep it approachable. Nine weights across upright and italic families, plus a single variable font, move it from powerful headlines to clean readable text.
foundry_blurb: Typeverything describe Claro as a versatile sans-serif with a bold, masculine presence, drawing on rugged 1890s New York truck lettering and blending historical grit with modern precision across its full weight range.

name: Mr Banks
classification_notes: The main Serif family within the Mr Banks release: angular terminals paired with round shapes for a display serif that reads as both classic and current. A separate single-style Stencil cut is bundled in the same release and split out as its own entry given the different construction.
summary: A seven-style display serif mixing angular terminals with round shapes, built for bold headlines and sports or packaging branding.
description: Mr Banks balances classic serif structure with modern rounding, its angular terminals and round shapes giving it timeless appeal without feeling dated. Numerous alternates suit sports branding and packaging as much as elegant headline or text use. Seven styles come with a variable font for the full family pack.
foundry_blurb: Typeverything describe Mr Banks as balancing classic design with modern aesthetics through angular terminals and round shapes, recommending it for sports, branding and packaging projects wanting timeless appeal with contemporary style.

name: Mr Banks Stencil
classification_notes: A single-style stencil cut bundled into the Mr Banks release, sharing its serif skeleton but broken into open, disconnected stencil forms. Split out here as a stencil face is a genuinely different construction to the main Serif family it ships alongside.
summary: A single heavyweight stencil cut of Mr Banks, breaking its serif skeleton into open, disconnected stencil forms for posters and branding.
description: Mr Banks Stencil takes the heaviest weight of the Mr Banks serif family and reworks it into a stencil structure, keeping the parent design's angular character while opening up the counters. It suits posters, packaging and branding work that wants a stencilled, industrial edge without leaving the Mr Banks family entirely.
foundry_blurb: Bundled within the Mr Banks release, the Stencil cut takes the family's heaviest weight and reworks it as a stencil, giving designers a bolder, more industrial option alongside the main serif styles.

name: Champ
classification_notes: A cheerful, approachable grotesque with a straightforward weight range, built for general branding and text use rather than a specific historical reference.
summary: A nine-weight friendly grotesque built for brand materials and logotypes, running from bold headline weights to more subtle text use.
description: Champ is a general-purpose grotesque built around a cheerful, approachable personality rather than a specific historical model. Nine weights cover everything from bold, impactful headlines to more restrained body text, with a variable font included in the full family pack for branding, logotype and website use.
foundry_blurb: Typeverything describe Champ as a versatile sans serif bringing fun and friendliness to branding, logotypes and websites, offering nine weights suited to both headline and text use.

name: Globo
classification_notes: An inclined titling sans built from brush-lettering research, developed as a more contemporary alternative to brush-script classics like Balloon or Banco while keeping the sturdy structure of a sans.
summary: An energetic inclined titling sans inspired by 1960s poster brush lettering, positioned as a modern alternative to classics like Balloon or Banco.
description: Globo grew from a single sketch of bold uppercase poster lettering found in a 1960 handbook for commercial artists. Though its roots are in brush lettering, the letterforms were given a solid, sturdy structure that reads as a proper sans rather than a script, making it a contemporary counterpart to brush-lettering classics. It suits sports, kids' products, food branding, music and streetwear work.
foundry_blurb: Typeverything describe Globo as an energetic inclined titling typeface developed from a 1960s handbook sketch of bold poster lettering, positioned as a modern alternative to brush-energy classics like Balloon or Banco.

name: Avena
classification_notes: A contemporary humanist sans with classic humanist proportions modernised for branding and editorial use, offered in matching upright and italic families.
summary: A seven-weight humanist sans blending elegance with an approachable personality, in matching upright and italic families.
description: Avena brings a modern touch to classic humanist proportions, aiming for elegance without losing warmth. Seven weights across Upright and Italic families come with extensive alternate characters, and full Latin Extended coverage keeps it usable across a wide range of branding and editorial applications.
foundry_blurb: Typeverything describe Avena as a contemporary humanist sans-serif blending elegance with a friendly personality, drawing on classic humanist proportions and offering extensive alternates for branding and editorial projects.

name: Cleric
classification_notes: An Art Nouveau-influenced serif drawing on early twentieth-century book cover lettering, spanning three widths (Condensed, Normal, Wide) each with a full weight range and variable font.
summary: An eighteen-style Art Nouveau serif across three widths, with elegant curves and graceful contrast drawn from early twentieth-century book covers.
description: Cleric takes its expressive curves and sense of movement from lettering found on early twentieth-century book covers, carrying real Art Nouveau spirit. Three widths, Condensed, Normal and Wide, each in six styles with a variable font, give it useful range for packaging, fashion and editorial design. Detailed letterforms and a flowing rhythm keep it warm without losing sophistication.
foundry_blurb: Typeverything describe Cleric as drawing on the expressive lettering of early twentieth-century book covers, carrying Art Nouveau spirit across three widths for packaging, fashion, editorial design and refined branding.

name: Figura
classification_notes: A rigorous grotesque sans built across three widths (Condensed, Normal, Wide), each in nine weights and interpolating across both axes in the full variable release.
summary: A twenty-seven-style rigorous grotesque spanning three widths and nine weights, built to interpolate freely across both axes.
description: Figura is a straightforward, rigorous grotesque sans offered across Condensed, Normal and Wide widths, each in nine weights. Owners of the full family can interpolate between both width and weight axes, making it a flexible, no-nonsense system for branding projects that need range without changing typeface.
foundry_blurb: Typeverything describe Figura as a brand new, rigorous sans serif built across three widths, each in nine weights, with full interpolation between axes for branding projects.

name: Friend
classification_notes: A condensed reworking of the classic Windsor typeface, offered as a single weight with a matching italic rather than a full weight range.
summary: A condensed serif reworking the classic Windsor design into a single weight with a matching italic, built for tight, space-conscious layouts.
description: Friend compacts the warm, approachable character of Windsor into a condensed form that fits space-conscious packaging and branding layouts without losing personality. It ships as a single weight with a corresponding italic, offering a compact alternative for bold headlines or tight spaces.
foundry_blurb: Typeverything describe Friend as a modern interpretation of the classic Windsor typeface, condensed to fit space-conscious layouts while keeping Windsor's warm, approachable nature for packaging and branding.

name: Grano
classification_notes: A geometric sans referencing Hermann Hoffmann's 1908 Block and Berthold's 1920 Schwere Block, offered in matching upright and italic families with a full weight range.
summary: An eighteen-style geometric block sans reworking two early twentieth-century Block typefaces, in matching upright and italic families.
description: Grano reimagines the classic Block typeface by Hermann Hoffmann and Berthold's Schwere Block with a contemporary twist, keeping the bold, well-defined character of both sources. Nine weights across upright and italic families give it a strong, confident presence suited to headlines, logotypes, packaging and other display applications where clarity matters.
foundry_blurb: Typeverything describe Grano as a modern geometric sans-serif inspired by Hermann Hoffmann's 1908 Block and Berthold's 1920 Schwere Block, reimagined with a contemporary twist for headlines, logotypes and packaging.

name: Talkie
classification_notes: Marketing copy does not name a specific historical reference or explicit category, but the weight structure and branding-first positioning match the foundry's other friendly grotesque sans faces such as Champ and Frizbee.
summary: An eighteen-style friendly grotesque in upright and italic families, built to bring contemporary flair to branding and packaging.
description: Talkie is a dynamic, general-purpose sans built to inject personality into branding and packaging work. Nine weights across upright and italic families come with a variable font for the full family pack, offering a versatile, approachable option in the same territory as the foundry's other friendly grotesques.
foundry_blurb: Typeverything describe Talkie as a fresh, dynamic typeface offering endless creative possibilities, recommending it for branding materials and packaging projects that want contemporary flair.

name: Niven
classification_notes: An elegant display serif named after actor David Niven, offered in matching upright and italic families with a particularly rich italic feature set.
summary: A ten-style elegant display serif named for David Niven, with an especially richly equipped italic full of ligatures and swash variants.
description: Niven takes its poise from the film presence of David Niven, built as an elegant display serif in matching Normal and Italic families across five weights each. The italic in particular carries dozens of ligatures and swash variants, giving it real range for editorial and branding use across a wide set of languages.
foundry_blurb: Typeverything describe Niven as a new elegant display serif inspired by the movies of David Niven, offered as upright and italic families with an italic rich in ligatures and swash variants.

name: Getty
classification_notes: A playful serif inspired by Cooper Black and 1970s serif conventions, with distinctly unconventional letterforms. Offered in matching upright and italic families.
summary: An eighteen-style rounded display serif inspired by Cooper Black, with playful, unconventional letterforms across upright and italic families.
description: Getty channels Cooper Black and the charm of 1970s serif design, but pushes into more unconventional letterform territory for a modern twist on the style. Nine weights across upright and italic families, plus variable files, give it a playful, warm personality well suited to logotypes and packaging.
foundry_blurb: Typeverything describe Getty as a fun, friendly typeface inspired by the iconic Cooper Black, with playful, rounded forms recommended for logotypes and packaging while echoing the charm of 1970s serif design.

name: Marques
classification_notes: A high-contrast display face with an atypical curve balance aimed at luxury packaging and branding; the marketing copy does not use the word serif but the described contrast and curve treatment sit in that tradition.
summary: A seven-weight high-contrast display face with an atypical curve balance, built for luxury packaging and branding work.
description: Marques is built for projects where elegance is the priority, using careful high contrast and an unusual curve balance to create a luxurious, exquisite personality. Seven weights come with a variable font in the full family pack, keeping it flexible for premium packaging and branding.
foundry_blurb: Typeverything describe Marques as a new display typeface built for packaging or branding projects where elegance is key, citing its careful high contrast and atypical curve balance as the source of its luxurious personality.

name: Frizbee
classification_notes: A fun, friendly grotesque explicitly described by the foundry as a sans, built with food packaging and kids' branding in mind.
summary: An eleven-weight friendly sans built to stand out in food packaging and to carry playful, kids'-focused branding.
description: Frizbee is a fun, friendly sans designed to bring joy to packaging and branding projects, with eleven weights covering a wide tonal range. A variable font is available in the full family pack, and the foundry positions it specifically for food packaging and children's branding that wants to feel different from the shelf norm.
foundry_blurb: Typeverything describe Frizbee as a new, fun and friendly sans built to bring joy to projects, calling it the secret sauce for food packaging that wants to stand out and the top pick for kids' branding.

name: Roast
classification_notes: Marketing copy keeps the description brief and does not name a specific category, but the weight structure and packaging-first positioning match the foundry's other friendly sans faces.
summary: A nine-weight friendly display sans with a summery, upbeat character, built for packshots and poster work.
description: Roast brings a summery, friendly vibe to display projects such as packaging, posters and branding. Nine weights are available for desktop or web use, with a variable font included in the full family pack, keeping it flexible across a range of display applications.
